_comment: Storyboard for the Grade 1 Mathematics unit lecture film, Days, Months and Clocks. Rendered by tools/create-ehel-unit-lecture.js. See lecture-video/BRIEF.md. Every beat is one narration clip; art.at names the phrases a picture waits for, and the page refuses to load if a phrase is not in its beat's say. The chapters follow the lesson opener's three parts (days and months; short times and long times; o'clock and half past), opened out with the lesson page's own examples: its seven day cards and the day after Wednesday (step 4), its twelve months and Hodan born in the first month (steps 5 and 11), its second-minute-hour-day-week ladder (steps 6 and 8), and its clocks - school at 8 o'clock, and the short hand between 3 and 4 at half past 3 (steps 7, 9 and 10).
title: Days, Months and Clocks
subtitle: Grade 1 Mathematics
objectives: Use familiar language to describe units of time.
Know the days of the week and the months of the year.
Recognise time to the hour and half hour.

beats.say: A week has seven days. A year has twelve months.
And a clock tells you the time, with two hands.
The days of the week always come round in the same order.
Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday.
Then Saturday, and then Sunday. That is seven days.
After Sunday the week starts again at Monday, round and round.
The day after Wednesday is Thursday. The day before Saturday is Friday.
A year is made of twelve months. They always come in this order.
January, February, March, April, May, June.
July, August, September, October, November, December.
The year starts at January and it ends at December.
Hodan was born in the first month. That month is January.
Some things take a very short time. Some take a very long time.
One clap takes about a second. That is the shortest.
Sixty seconds make one minute. A minute is longer.
One lesson at school lasts about an hour. That is sixty minutes.
A day is one whole sleep to the next sleep. That is much longer.

at.sleep: one whole sleep to the next

beats.say: A week is seven days. That is the longest one here.
A clock has two hands. They do two different jobs.
The short hand is the hour hand. It tells you the hour.
The long hand tells you how far through the hour you are.
Always look for the short hand first, every single time.
The long hand is bigger, but it never tells the hour.
At o'clock, the long hand points straight up to twelve.
Here the short hand is on the three. It is three o'clock.
School starts at eight o'clock. The short hand points to eight.
At half past, the long hand points straight down to six.
Now the short hand sits between two numbers on the face.
It is between three and four. So it is half past three.
Seven days make a week. Twelve months make a year.
A second is short. A whole year is long. Pick the right word.
Long hand up is o'clock. Long hand down is half past.
And the short hand always tells you the hour, every time.
